_comment: Hand corrections to the reader's output for A15, in pixels of the
full-resolution crops in .build/a15/ (see imageSize / sheetImageSize).
The reader placed 148 of the 236 designators (63%). Every marker was
reviewed by eye, tier by tier, against the drawing, and the tiers behave
very differently on this board:
agreed      83 of 90 right
single      24 of 25 right
ambiguous    9 of 13 right
collision    9 of 20 right
So 125 of 148 machine placements survived review. The 23 that did not were
all the same failure -- the marker sat on a neighbouring designator whose
label differs by one glyph (CR5 on CR9, R22 on CR22, C4 on C42, R8 on R82,
K6 on K9, R1 on R61). Each is moved onto its own label rather than dropped,
because the part is genuinely on the board a short distance away.
Three of the 23 are a different case and are not moved: H7, MP8 and MP9 are
a screw and two snap standoffs with no silkscreen designator at all. The
reader had truncated 'R80' and 'CR24' into them. They go to notOnDrawing,
which is where every other H and MP part on this board already is -- the
drawing labels no screw, rivet, standoff, cover, shield, insulator, cable
tie or ejector.
All eleven test points are placed by hand, spanning label and pad together,
and TP2, TP9, TP10 and TP11 carry a note about how their pad is drawn.

_notOnDrawingComment: Screws, rivets, spacers, insulators, ejectors and the rest of the hardware:
none of it is drawn on the locator, so counting it as unplaced would make
the coverage badge lie. It stays searchable in the parts list.
Q1 is here for a different reason -- it is not a part at all. It comes from
the Rev 9 scan alone, and review.txt reports it as sharing a row with Q11,
stock 454041, which did join. Reading that row off the Rev 9 page settles
it: the reference cell says 'Q 11' and nothing else, quantity 1, and the
1996 table has no Q1 either. The OCR split the two digits of Q11. Nothing
on the drawing or on either sheet carries a Q1, which is why the reader
never found one and a search of the artwork does not either.
_sheetsComment: Grid frames, measured corner by corner on each sheet at full resolution.
They are not the same: sheet 2's frame sits about 1.3% narrower than sheet
1's and further left, which is also why the two sheets are cropped
separately. On both sheets the outer border's left edge is at or beyond
x=0 in the scan, so the left-hand row letters are clipped; the frame below
is the inner zone border, which is what a zone reference is measured from.
The legend box on sheet 1 prints its own zone for every test point --
'TP1 = INPUT (PG1D7)' is sheet 1 zone D7 -- so the derived zones can be
checked against the sheet's own arithmetic rather than taken on trust.
_dropSchematicComment: Both sheets were reviewed marker by marker against the artwork. Sheet 1
kept 83 of 103 reads and sheet 2 kept 86 of 120 -- and the two sheets fail
in quite different ways.
Sheet 2's failures are almost all one block: the row of relay and transistor
pinout legends across the bottom right. 'Q4,Q15,Q16,Q22,Q23,Q24' and
'K6,K7,K10,K11,K14' printed as captions beside bottom-view symbols read to
the reader as nineteen placements, several passes agree on them, and they
arrive in the agreed tier looking like the best markers on the sheet. Those
parts are genuinely on the sheet -- their contacts and their symbols are
drawn in the circuit -- so the designator is right and only the position is
wrong, which is the case no parts-list check can catch. All nineteen are
dropped rather than nudged.
Sheet 1 has no such block; its failures are spread out and are the ordinary
schematic misreads. The HR7 ASSY pin-number strip along the bottom supplies
three of them on its own (pin 9 read as Q9, pin 8 as C18, pin 2 as U2), and
the rest are a value ('1/4W' as L4, '1M' as L5, '0.1' as U1, '10uF' as C7),
a net name ('HV C6*' as C6, 'PACOM' as MP8, 'GUARD' as MP4), a pin label
('3A' as H8, '11' as R1, '19' as VR8), or a word of a caption ('INPUT' as
U5, 'DETAIL 1' as MP7, 'PREAMP' as MP3, 'RST' as R57).
Both sheets draw an oven cover as a four-pin block -- 'LARGE OVEN COVER' on
sheet 1 beside HR7, 'OVEN COVER' on sheet 2 beside H4 -- and the reader put
MP4 on one and MP5 on the other. Table 6-19 calls MP4 'MOLDED COVER, REF.
HYBRID' and MP5 'MOLDED COVER, HYBRID, R-NET', and it is HR7 that is the
hybrid bonded to an R-net, so the reader's pairing is more likely backwards
than right. Both are dropped: an unplaced part is better than a confidently
mislabelled one. MP3 is kept, because sheet 2 draws it as 'REAR SHIELD' and
there is only one of those.
Test points are the other systematic failure and they are placed by hand.
TP1 and TP5 belong on sheet 1 and TP9 and TP10 on sheet 2; the reader put
TP1 on 'TIP120', TP5 on TP9's own flag, and never found TP9 or TP10 at all.
Each hand placement is checked against the zone the sheet 1 legend prints
for it -- TP1 = INPUT (PG1D7), TP5 = BUFFER (PG1C4), TP9 = VI + (PG2B6),
TP10 = VI - (PG2A6) -- and all four derive the zone the legend states.
U1, U2 and Q9 are placed by hand on sheet 1 for the same reason: §5-21 names
all three, so a marker that lands on an HR7 pin number is worse than useless.
_schematicComment: Hand placements in pixels of .build/a15/sch1_full.png and sch2_full.png.
Everything here was measured off a labelled pixel grid and, for the test
points, cross-checked against the zone the sheet 1 legend prints.
A later pass placed the 35 remaining electrical parts that had no
schematic position, 18 on sheet 1 and 17 on sheet 2. Most of them were
sitting in the reader's collision tier, which build_coords.py discards
outright: two designators read at one pixel, one of them the label that
is actually printed there. C10 not C19, C41 not C4, CR24 not R24, Q4 not
U4, Q8 not C8, C21 not C2, C40 not C4 -- in every case the collision was
at the right pixel and only the choice of name was open, so each was
settled by looking at the crop and the part number printed under it.
Two of the dropped reads turned out to be the neighbouring part rather
than a misread of something else: sheet 1's 'C2' at (3173,786) is C4's
label, and sheet 1's 'CR12' at (5344,2776) is CR10's. Both drops stay,
and the two parts are now placed by hand at those pixels.
Q1 is the one part still unplaced. It is a TO-220, 100V, 2W, qty 1 in
Table 6-19, and it is not drawn on either sheet: neither reader found a
Q1 anywhere, and a zone-by-zone read of both sheets lists only Q3, Q4,
Q6, Q8, Q9, Q20 and Q21 on sheet 1 and Q10-Q16, Q18, Q19, Q22-Q24 on
sheet 2 (plus the bottom-view legend captions, which are dropped). It has
no board position either.

C2.note: 0.01uF in the +HV sense return, immediately left of R5.

C4.note: 0.022uF 1500V in series with R4 off K5A. The reader read this same label as C2, which is why C2 is dropped on this sheet.

C6.note: 0.047uF to SCOM beside R21 in the preamp diagnostic net. The reader's only C6 read was the net name 'HV C6*'.

C8.note: 680pF to ACOM on the ac sense line, one net above C10. The reader's C8 read landed on Q8's label instead.

C10.note: 680pF below C8. Read here as a C10/C19 collision; C10 is what is printed.

C41.note: 0.22uF on Q4's emitter in the current-limit circuit. Read here as a C4/C41 collision; C41 is what is printed.

CR10.note: 1N4002 beside CR9 on the HV SENSE return. The reader read this same label as CR12, which is why CR12 is dropped on this sheet.

CR21.note: Hand-lettered 5.3mA current-regulator diode across CR4/CR18 to -15S.

CR24.note: 1N4448 from U1 pin 7 to pin 6. Read here as a CR24/R24 collision; CR24 is what is printed.

Q4.note: 2N3904, the CUR LIM driver. Read here as a Q4/U4 collision; Q4 is what is printed and U4 is on sheet 2.

Q8.note: TIP32A in the HR7 heater control, with C14 on its +8RLH supply. Read here as a C8/Q8 collision.

Q20.note: J2656 FET beside Q21 inside DETAIL 1. Its only agreed read was in sheet 2's pinout legend and was dropped.

R9.note: 1M across R8, above the C7/R10 pair in the ac sense feedback.

R24.note: 10 ohm off the +SP C node beside TP6. The reader's R24 read collided with CR24's label instead.

R31.note: 2k 1/2W in the +44 S feed, above VR3.

R32.note: 2k 1/2W in the -44 S feed, below VR4.

VR3.note: 20V zener on the +20 S rail below R31.

TP9.note: The VI+ flag. Derived zone B6 agrees with the sheet 1 legend's 'TP9 = VI + (PG2B6)'.

TP10.note: The VI- flag. Derived zone A6 agrees with the sheet 1 legend's 'TP10 = VI - (PG2A6)'.

C21.note: 0.1uF on U3A's -15S pin. Read here as a C2/C21 collision; C21 is what is printed.

C40.note: 0.1uF from VI COM to VI -, right of C39. Read here as a C4/C40 collision; C40 is what is printed.

CR12.note: 1N4448 from U3A pin 3 to SCOM, right of R44. Sheet 1's CR12 read was really CR10 and is dropped there.

CR13.note: 1N4448 from SCOM into the R53/R54 divider under Q16.

R37.note: 825 MF in the G+ line, left of C18.

R83.note: 4.7K in the VI + line into Q24.

U4.note: LF356 with C26 and C27 on its supplies. The reader's only U4 read was on sheet 1, on Q4's label.

_dropComment: Reader placements on parts that have no silkscreen designator at all.
notOnDrawing alone would not remove them: it says the part has no marker to
find, while the bogus marker would still be drawn, and the coverage badge
would count the part as placed. H7 was read off a pad stroke above R28;
MP8 and MP9 are truncations of R80 and CR24.
_layersComment: Alignment of the photograph to board space. Nothing covers this board in the
photograph -- the rear shield is off -- but the two hybrid covers and the two
heat sinks are fitted, so HR7, H4, Z5, Z6, Q11, Q14 and the parts under the
covers are hidden even though their positions are right.
The eight landmark pairs below were read off labelled pixel grids on both
images: the ends of the test point row and TP11 along the top, the K9/K6/K11
relay cluster at bottom left, P602 at bottom right and K10 up the right-hand
side. That is a spread of the whole board, but every pair is a label centre
judged by eye rather than a measured fiducial, and the photograph is not a
perfectly overhead shot, so the fit is marked approximate. Expect a marker to
land on the right part and not necessarily on the middle of it.
